title: Tensor Product Dehn Invariant in ℝ ⊗_ℚ (ℝ/πℚ)
description: Formalizes the proper tensor product Dehn invariant D(P) ∈ ℝ ⊗_ℚ (ℝ/πℚ) using algebraic tensor products in Lean 4, and proves that the cube and regular tetrahedron have distinct invariants — completing the invariant separation in the correct algebraic setting.

originalContributions: Defines piRatSpan = span_ℚ{π} ⊂ ℝ as the ℚ-rational multiples of π — the correct modulus for the Dehn invariant
Defines angleClass : ℝ → ℝ ⧸ piRatSpan sending angle θ to its class [θ] in ℝ/πℚ
Defines dehnElement : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ ⊗_ℚ (ℝ/πℚ) as n ⊗ [θ], representing n edges of dihedral angle θ
Proves one_tmul_ne_zero: for any ℚ-module M and m ≠ 0, the element 1 ⊗ₜ m is nonzero in ℝ ⊗_ℚ M — via a separating ℚ-linear functional
Proves cube_dehn_zero: D(cube) = 12 ⊗ [π/2] = 0 since π/2 ∈ πℚ
Proves tetra_dehn_ne_zero: D(tetrahedron) = 6 ⊗ [arccos(1/3)] ≠ 0 since arccos(1/3) ∉ πℚ

meta.assumptions: 0 axioms, 0 sorries. The proof uses Classical.choice (standard Lean axiom) via Module.Free.chooseBasis to construct a separating ℚ-linear functional; this is not a mathematical axiom but a foundational logic axiom present in all Lean proofs. The irrationality of arccos(1/3)/π is inherited from tetrahedron_angle_irrational_pi in the parent file (DissectionOfCubesOQ02.lean), which is fully proved via Chebyshev recurrence.

overview.historicalContext: Max Dehn (1900) defined his invariant as D(P) = Σ_e ℓ(e) ⊗ [θ(e)] ∈ ℝ ⊗_ℤ (ℝ/πℤ), where the sum is over all edges e of polyhedron P, ℓ(e) is the edge length, and [θ(e)] is the dihedral angle mod πℤ. The key property is that scissors-congruent polyhedra have equal Dehn invariants. The cube has all dihedral angles π/2 = (1/2)π ∈ πℚ, so its invariant is zero. The regular tetrahedron has dihedral angle arccos(1/3) ∉ πℚ (by Niven's theorem), giving a nonzero invariant. This formalization replaces ℤ with ℚ as the scalar ring — equivalent for polyhedra with rational edge lengths — enabling use of ℚ-vector space structure (in particular, existence of separating functionals) to prove the tetrahedron's invariant is nonzero.
overview.problemStatement: Formalize the tensor product Dehn invariant D(P) ∈ ℝ ⊗_ℚ (ℝ/πℚ) in Lean 4 using Mathlib's TensorProduct machinery, and prove that the cube and regular tetrahedron have distinct invariants via D(cube) = 0 ≠ D(tetrahedron).
overview.text: This entry formalizes the proper algebraic tensor product Dehn invariant for Hilbert's Third Problem. Unlike the parent entry (which uses a simplified boolean predicate), this formalization places the invariant in its correct algebraic home: the ℚ-tensor product ℝ ⊗_ℚ (ℝ/πℚ). The key mathematical content is proving that 6 ⊗ [arccos(1/3)] ≠ 0 in this tensor product, which requires showing that the class [arccos(1/3)] is nonzero in ℝ/πℚ and that tensoring a nonzero element with 1 ∈ ℝ preserves nonzero-ness — a consequence of ℝ being faithfully flat over ℚ.
overview.proofStrategy: Three-layer proof. Layer 1 (algebraic setup): Define piRatSpan = ℚ·π ⊂ ℝ as a Submodule, and angleClass as the quotient map ℝ → ℝ ⧸ piRatSpan. Layer 2 (angle separation): Prove cube_angle_class_zero (π/2 ∈ piRatSpan → class = 0) and tetra_angle_class_ne_zero (arccos(1/3) ∉ piRatSpan → class ≠ 0, using tetrahedron_angle_irrational_pi from the parent). Layer 3 (tensor product nonzero): The general lemma one_tmul_ne_zero proves that 1 ⊗ₜ m ≠ 0 in ℝ ⊗_ℚ M whenever m ≠ 0. Proof: Since M is a ℚ-vector space (free ℚ-module), choose a basis and extract a coordinate functional φ with φ(m) ≠ 0; apply id ⊗ φ to map 1 ⊗ m to 1·φ(m) ≠ 0 in ℝ. Combining: dehnElement n θ = n ⊗ [θ]; n=6 and [arccos(1/3)] ≠ 0 gives nonzero Dehn invariant for tetrahedron; n=12 and [π/2] = 0 gives zero invariant for cube.
keyInsights: The correct algebraic home for the Dehn invariant is ℝ ⊗_ℤ (ℝ/πℤ), but working over ℚ (ℝ ⊗_ℚ (ℝ/πℚ)) is equivalent for polyhedra with rational edge lengths and gives access to ℚ-vector space theory
The hardest step is proving 1 ⊗ m ≠ 0 for m ≠ 0 in ℝ ⊗_ℚ M — this requires the axiom of choice (to find a separating functional) and reflects the faithfully flat extension ℚ → ℝ
The angle class [θ] = 0 in ℝ/πℚ iff θ is a rational multiple of π — precisely the distinction between cube (π/2 = (1/2)π) and tetrahedron (arccos(1/3)/π irrational by Niven)
Using Mathlib's TensorProduct.mk and Submodule.mkQ enables clean proof of both cube_dehn_zero (via simp after rewriting the class to 0) and tetra_dehn_ne_zero (via smul_ne_zero and one_tmul_ne_zero)

The use of Module.Free.chooseBasis to extract a separating ℚ-linear functional is an instance of a general principle: over a field (or PID), any nonzero element of a free module can be distinguished from zero by a coordinate functional — this is precisely the content of faithful flatness of ℚ → ℝ as an extension of commutative rings
prerequisites: Tensor products over commutative rings (ℚ-bilinear maps)
Quotient modules and the universal property
Niven's theorem: arccos(1/3) is an irrational multiple of π
Free modules and basis existence over ℚ (axiom of choice)

sections.title: Module Setup and Imports
sections.summary: Imports Mathlib and the parent proof DissectionOfCubesOQ02 (which contains tetrahedron_angle_irrational_pi via Chebyshev recurrence). Opens the Real and DissectionOfCubesOQ02 namespaces. The module docstring states the OQ-02-WIP-01 goal: formalize the proper algebraic tensor product Dehn invariant in ℝ ⊗_ℚ (ℝ/πℚ), completing what the parent entry proves with a simplified boolean predicate.
sections.mathContext: Key import: `Proofs.DissectionOfCubesOQ02` provides `tetrahedron_angle_irrational_pi : ¬∃ q : ℚ, arccos (1/3) = q * π`, the Niven-type irrationality result proved via Chebyshev polynomial recurrence in the parent file. This is the sole dependency bridging analysis (irrationality) to algebra (tensor products).

sections.title: Tensor Product Setup
sections.summary: Defines the three fundamental objects: piRatSpan (the ℚ-span of π inside ℝ as a ℚ-submodule), angleClass (the quotient map ℝ → ℝ ⧸ piRatSpan sending each angle to its class mod πℚ), and dehnElement (n ⊗ [θ] in ℝ ⊗_ℚ (ℝ/πℚ), representing n edges of dihedral angle θ).
sections.mathContext: piRatSpan := $\{q \cdot \pi \mid q \in \mathbb{Q}\} \subset \mathbb{R}$ as a $\mathbb{Q}$-submodule. angleClass $\theta := [\theta] \in \mathbb{R}/\pi\mathbb{Q}$. dehnElement $n$ $\theta := n \cdot (1 \otimes_{\mathbb{Q}} [\theta]) \in \mathbb{R} \otimes_{\mathbb{Q}} (\mathbb{R}/\pi\mathbb{Q})$.

sections.title: Cube and Tetrahedron Angle Classes
sections.summary: Proves that π/2 ∈ piRatSpan (since π/2 = (1/2)·π) and hence [π/2] = 0 in ℝ/πℚ. Also proves that arccos(1/3) ∉ piRatSpan (directly from tetrahedron_angle_irrational_pi) and hence [arccos(1/3)] ≠ 0.

sections.title: Tensor Product Nonzero Lemma
sections.summary: Proves the key general lemma: for any ℚ-module M and nonzero m : M, the element 1 ⊗ₜ m is nonzero in ℝ ⊗_ℚ M. The proof extracts a separating ℚ-linear functional φ : M → ℚ with φ(m) ≠ 0 using Module.Free.chooseBasis, then applies id ⊗ φ to separate 1 ⊗ m from 0.

sections.title: Dehn Invariant Computation and Separation
sections.summary: Proves cube_dehn_zero: D(cube) = 12 ⊗ [π/2] = 0 (since [π/2] = 0). Proves tetra_dehn_ne_zero: D(tetrahedron) = 6 ⊗ [arccos(1/3)] ≠ 0 (since 6 ≠ 0 and [arccos(1/3)] ≠ 0 by one_tmul_ne_zero). Concludes dehn_invariants_differ.

conclusion.summary: This formalization places the Dehn invariant in its correct algebraic setting: the tensor product ℝ ⊗_ℚ (ℝ/πℚ). The key contributions are (1) the general one_tmul_ne_zero lemma showing nonzero elements remain nonzero after tensoring with 1 ∈ ℝ, and (2) the complete computation showing D(cube) = 0 ≠ D(tetrahedron) in this tensor product. This upgrades the boolean invariant in the parent entry to a proper algebraic invariant, connecting to the algebraic K-theory interpretation of scissors congruence groups.
conclusion.implications: The tensor product Dehn invariant formalization demonstrates the power of Mathlib's algebraic infrastructure: Submodule quotients, tensor products, and free module bases combine cleanly to produce a rigorous treatment of a classical geometric theorem. The one_tmul_ne_zero lemma is a general result about faithful flatness of field extensions that may be useful in other formalization contexts.
